property_definitions.definition: The full proposition in this source account, including its conditions. Its presence does not assert its truth or endorsement.
Source-declared force of the proposition in this account, such as hypothetical or denied; separate from the truth and review of its description.
What reasoning is reconstructed and which limits remain; not an automatic interpretation of graph structure.
Partial, claimed_complete or unknown coverage of this argument. Claimed completeness is not mechanically proved.
The described inferential transition, not a proof that the transition preserves truth.
The source account's description of the reasoning mode; it does not select executable inference code.
What is challenged and why. Targets are separate grounded Claims; no negation of a target is inferred merely from a challenge.
The described scope and limits of this research referent; it is not a canonical definition, historical date, or causal assertion.
The explicit research criterion for retaining this semantic subject through corrected descriptions; shared names or equal record versions are not identity evidence.
Source-declared calendar, not an inferred conversion. A missing or null value is not Gregorian.
What the dating concerns. Historical time is separate from witness creation, data capture and knowledge revision.
Exact, approximate, uncertain or unknown date value. Exactness at the declared precision is not evidence that the enclosing Claim is true or accepted.
Original year-numbering declaration. Unsupported or unknown numbering is preserved without conversion to astronomical years.
Source-declared before, after, during or overlaps relative to a resolved anchor, not an inferred absolute date or causal edge.
Inclusive lower date key: astronomical year * 10000 + month * 100 + day, proleptic Gregorian only. Not a timestamp or duration; absent for unparsed or incompatible calendars.
Inclusive upper date key widened to source precision. Intersect [a,b] with start <= b AND end >= a. Missing bounds are unknown, not infinite.
Readable projected title; never an identity key.
Declared review state; not-recorded explicitly means no state was supplied, not acceptance.
Registered type closure, including this type. Contains selects a type and all its descendants.
Source-declared interval start; precision and calendar remain separate qualifiers.
Source-declared interval end; absent means unknown, not infinite.
Source-owned assertion version, distinct from entity identity and projection content revision.

types.definition: A proposition identified as content under examination, with its conditions and declared assertion force. Its formulation and truth are distinct; premise and conclusion are roles of a thesis within a specific inferential step, and a Claim about a thesis is a separate research assertion.

An identified reasoning structure described or reconstructed from evidence, possibly incompletely. Its inferential steps, targeted thesis and objections are grounded relations; neither connectedness nor an argument label proves validity, soundness or an author's endorsement.

An identified transition within an account of reasoning. Premises and conclusions are context-bound role claims pointing to theses. A step can be examined or challenged without accepting its premises, rule or result, and logical reconstruction order is distinct from historical time.

An identified challenge with substantive reasons and explicit target relations. A challenge to one premise or transition is distinct from rejection of an entire argument or conception. Its presence does not establish that the challenge succeeds or that its author is hostile.

A research referent whose explicit continuity criterion allows different situated conceptions without identifying their definitions. It is neither a bare shared name nor one definition imposed on all accounts. Membership requires grounded, contestable claims; existing scoped Concept nodes are not silently promoted to this subtype.

A situated account of thought with its own referent identity and substantive description. Attribution, conceptual membership and expression need separate grounded claims. A historical transformation relates distinct conceptions; a corrected description increments this record version without creating a new conception. A language form or a Claim about the conception is not the conception.

A persistent communicative or documentary intellectual object that need not be a Work. Its identity is distinct from a physical carrier, textual realization, catalog record and digital file. Corrected descriptions do not create another document; an attribution of shared content or identity requires a separate claim.

A document constituted as addressed correspondence. Sender, addressee, author, dispatch and reception are distinct context-bound claims, not subclasses or mandatory known facts. An unsent draft may be correspondence without an asserted dispatch; a copy is not automatically the same carrier or another letter.

A persistent physical source-object identity, including a manuscript carrier. It is not its inventory number, catalog record, intellectual work, reconstructed composite, transcription or digital representation. Description changes do not change the artifact ID. Source metadata navigation alone does not assert any carrier-to-text, custody or historical relation.
Root for source-described happenings, developments and persisting conditions in the historical world; not semantic Event/State, a dating assertion, or a provenance activity.

A source-described occurrence treated as one happening. Its identity is independent of labels, disputed dating, participants, and correction of its description. An interpretation of its significance is a separate claim.
A source-described temporally developing process. Its phases, participants, and relation to events require claims; a long event is not retyped by duration alone.
A source-described persisting condition in a historical scope. It is not an authored semantic State, an absence inferred from missing events, or a causal explanation.
Exact version-bound text-layer representation; not the underlying Work.
Version-bound source selector. Offsets belong to this exact layer, not a mutable document.
A source-layout or method-proposed unit. Unit kind and boundary posture remain qualifiers, never lexical identity.
A particular attested occurrence addressed through exact source anchors.
Source-declared lexical identity independent of spelling variants, label, and philosophical concept.
Context-dependent lexical reading, distinct from a lexeme and a philosophical concept.
Source-declared sign identity with its admission status and competing interpretations.
Versioned stand-off annotation or segmentation packet; not source-text authority.
Claim under the semantic annotation v2 contract, preserving proposition, evidence, maker, alternatives and review refs.
Evidence for an annotation claim with direction, role and exact source anchors.
Source-owned review event scoped to claims or segmentations; never inferred from a status label.
An addressable source relation assertion linked to its exact supporting claim.
Root of the semantic interchange hierarchy; it does not assert one philosophical ontology.
An object whose ToS identity persists while versioned descriptions and assertions may change.
A persistent person-like responsibility bearer; author, translator and editor remain relation roles rather than subclasses.
A persistent collective or institutional identity participating in source claims.
Root for persistent intellectual creations, communicative documents, realizations and aggregates. The bibliographic ladder is one profile under this root, not a required shape for every document.
An abstract intellectual or artistic creation, distinct from language realization, edition, acquired item and file.
A language- or version-specific realization of one Work.
Root for edition and collection identities that embody or aggregate Expressions and Works.
A published or edited manifestation, distinct from one acquired copy.
An aggregate publication or container with evidence-bearing membership claims.
One physical or digital acquired copy or container.
One immutable byte sequence addressed by its declared digest.
A versioned observed access or authority link; it is not the object it points to.
Root for authored ToS node classes; it does not make branch candidates canonical.
An authored source-grounded semantic node, distinct from a bibliographic Work or source file.
A source-returnable concept node or an explicitly pre-canon concept candidate.
An authored principle node.
An authored lineage or movement path between semantic objects.
An authored semantic event; event identity is distinct from its temporal assertions.
An authored semantic state.
An authored support or contextual grounding node.
An authored contextual node.
An authored analogy node.
An authored reviewed synthesis node.
A versioned assertion whose identity, evidence and review posture remain separate from its subject and object.
A reified evidence-bearing assertion with its own version, maker, provenance and review state.
Root for explicit temporal assertions, instants and intervals; raw period labels remain unparsed candidates.
A claim-scoped temporal value with an explicit calendar, facet, precision and uncertainty posture where available.
A normalized point-like temporal value within a declared calendar and precision.
A normalized start/end temporal value with separate boundary precision and meaning.
A claim-scoped publication, manufacture or distribution activity preserving literal statement, roles, places and time.
A value scoped to a claim and not promoted into persistent identity.
A literal place statement kept distinct from a normalized Place identity.
Root for evidence, review, provenance and maker representations supporting claims.
A source-returnable evidence reference supporting or challenging a claim.
A distinct review event or decision over an assertion.
A versioned activity recording how a source or claim representation was produced.
The recorded human, model or system responsibility representation that made a claim.
Root for normalized place identity and claim-scoped spatial references; navigation Regions remain separate.
A persistent normalized Place identity; its names, boundaries and historical validity remain versioned assertions.
A tree or atlas navigation object that must not be mistaken for a persistent domain identity.
A branch-shaped navigation object in the source tree.
An atlas era route; it is not by itself a normalized temporal interval.
A branch region used for navigation; it is not automatically a geographic Place or containment fact.
A source-tree tradition route.
A pre-canon philosophy projection category for a school or tradition.
A source-owned link between a philosophy branch and a source-witness backlog anchor.
A source-facing witness identity not yet resolved to a more specific public semantic type.
Root for pre-canon philosophy atlas categories; these types stabilize interchange without canonizing instances.
A pre-canon figure anchor, not yet necessarily a normalized Agent identity.
A pre-canon institution category, distinct from a normalized Organization record.
A pre-canon text-corpus category, not a Work, Collection or acquired Item by implication.
A pre-canon controversy or contested-reading category.
A pre-canon genre classification candidate.
A pre-canon medium category.
A pre-canon combined language or script category; normalization may later split the two.
A pre-canon transmission channel category.
A pre-canon method category.
A pre-canon preservation-state category.
A pre-canon combined civilization or literary-complex category.
A pre-canon object whose chronology, geography or evidence posture cannot yet be represented as an ordinary branch.
A pre-canon artifact navigation anchor, not a normalized physical artifact identity by implication.
Atlas, graph-view, table and dossier projection metadata rather than a domain entity.
A repository topology or resource representation, never the domain object described by its file.
The root of the repository topology projection.
A branch representation from the ToS source-home manifest.
A manifest-file representation in the repository topology.
A file or generated-resource representation in the repository projection.
A projection placeholder whose source-local endpoint exists but whose full entity representation is not available in this carrier.
Explicit fallback for a source-native kind that has no reviewed semantic interchange mapping yet.
